g.title: startup
g.text: How to start the project (new machine, or a machine that has run it before)

g.title: cluster_old
g.text: MACHINE THAT HAS RUN THE PROJECT (about 1 minute)

g.title: start
g.text: You want to run the project

g.title: setup
g.text: Has this PC run the project before?
(WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Docker and the folder ~/slb all exist)

g.title: n0
g.text: Settings > Time and language > Sync now
(a wrong clock makes experiment runs invalid)

g.title: e0
g.text: 1. Check the Windows clock is synced

g.title: n2
g.text: -> installs Docker, containerlab and tshark inside Ubuntu
-> builds the images -> deploys the lab -> starts the UI

g.title: e1a
g.text: wsl -d Ubuntu -u root systemctl stop docker docker.socket
(two distros share one network and would clash)

g.title: e2a
g.text: wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root systemctl start docker
(quick_start.bat also wakes WSL, which starts Docker by itself)

g.title: e3
g.text: Keep its window open: it keeps WSL awake

g.title: dnote
g.text: Docker is a service that runs inside Ubuntu 24.04 (not Docker Desktop).
It starts by itself when WSL starts and stops when WSL shuts down
(WSL shuts itself down when nothing is running in it).
When Docker restarts, the lab containers come back WITHOUT their
network links: the check below catches this and the fix is a rebuild.
Do not run Docker in two Ubuntu distros at once.

g.title: c2
g.text: Traceroute c1 to b1 shows exactly

g.title: c5
g.text: What do you want to do?

g.title: c6
g.text: UI panel U13: Start load, wait 20 s,
Try the algorithms and the delay buttons

g.title: c7
g.text: Close the UI and heavy programs,

g.title: stop
g.text: close the quick_start window -> bash topo/teardown.sh -> wsl --shutdown
